questions.q: What is a Release Update, as distinct from a regular new feature in a seasonal release?
options: A cosmetic UI change with no functional effect
A paid add-on an org must purchase separately
A change to existing platform behavior — often security or performance related — that Salesforce intends to eventually make mandatory for every org
A feature that only affects sandboxes, never production
questions.explain: Unlike most new, additive, opt-in features, Release Updates change how existing platform behavior works, and Salesforce plans to enforce them for every org eventually — which is why they ship with a deadline and a test period.

questions.q: What happens if an admin never reviews a pending release update before its Complete Steps By date?
options: The update is cancelled automatically
Salesforce activates the update automatically once the date passes, whether or not it was reviewed
The org is locked out of Setup until the admin responds
Nothing — release updates never activate without explicit admin approval
questions.explain: Complete Steps By is a real deadline — once it passes, Salesforce activates the update automatically, which is exactly why reviewing it in advance matters.

questions.q: What does Enable Test Run let an admin do?
options: Permanently disable a release update forever
Automatically roll the update out to every connected sandbox
Skip the update entirely without any record of it
Turn the update on or off in the org during its test period (which ends on the Complete Steps By date) to observe its real impact before committing
questions.explain: Enable Test Run exists specifically so an admin can see the real effect of a release update on their org before the deadline forces the decision.

questions.q: What replaced the older 'Critical Updates' console in Salesforce Setup?
options: Release Updates, which includes more detailed information about upcoming changes than the old console did
Field Audit Trail
Setup Audit Trail
Change Sets
questions.explain: Release Updates is the modern replacement for the Critical Updates console, with more detail about each change, step-by-step actions, and a test run option.

questions.q: Why does the lesson describe Release Updates as 'one of the few Setup pages genuinely worth checking on a recurring schedule'?
options: Because it's the only page that shows billing information
Because it must be checked daily or the org is suspended
Because updates there activate on Salesforce's own timeline once their deadline passes, so an org that never checks it risks an unreviewed behavior change landing without warning
Because it's the only way to see which users are currently logged in
questions.explain: An update left unreviewed still activates automatically at its Complete Steps By date — checking the page regularly is how an admin avoids being surprised by a change that was fully documented in advance but never read.
